How to use this calculator

  1. Enter initial investment, ending value, holding period.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How interest rate is calculated

Annualized growth assumes the entire change occurred at one steady compound rate and ignores interim deposits or withdrawals. Total ROI, when shown, compares gain with the initial amount. Formula: Annualized rate = (ending value ÷ starting value)^(1 ÷ years) − 1. Use the displayed details to inspect the intermediate amounts and replace example assumptions with terms from your own quote or records.

Annualized rate = (ending value ÷ starting value)^(1 ÷ years) − 1.
A worked example

Growing from $1,000 to $1,210 in 2 years implies a 10% annual compound return.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Financial projections use your assumptions. Actual returns, lender terms, fees and tax rules can differ; these results do not guarantee a future outcome.

Frequently asked questions

Interest Rate Calculator: what does the result include?

No. Annualized return expresses a multi-year change as one compound rate per year; total return measures the whole gain over the holding period.

Interest Rate Calculator: which assumptions matter most?

No. The calculation compares only the entered initial and ending values. Use an investment projection when regular contributions matter.
